Bug_Title: EOS: Data read is converted before comparison to -1 (EOS_BAD_END_OF_STREAM_CHECK)
Bug_Details:
The method java.io.FileInputStream.read() returns an int. If this int is converted to a byte then -1 (which
indicates an EOF) and the byte 0xFF become indistinguishable, this comparing the (converted) result to -1
causes the read (probably in a loop) to end prematurely if the character 0xFF is met. Similarly, the method
java.io.FileReader.read() also returns an int. If it is converted to a char then -1 becomes 0xFFFF which is
Character.MAX_VALUE. Comparing the result to -1 is pointless, since characters are unsigned in Java. If the
checking for EOF is the condition of a loop then this loop is infinite. 
See SEI CERT rule FIO08-J. Distinguish between characters or bytes read from a stream and -1.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the while loop condition where the int returned by inputStream.read() is cast to byte before comparison with -1. This can cause the loop to prematurely terminate if the byte value read is -1 (EOF) or 0xFF.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the byte value 0xFF is read from the file. This byte value is converted to -1 due to casting to byte before comparison with -1 in the while loop condition. This causes the loop to prematurely terminate, resulting in an incorrect string being returned.
